subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for Aperture Labs pilot: tokens/sec, SLO fit, headroom
messages:
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@aperturelabs.com>

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for our MVP pilot

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick intro on the call earlier — excited to explore Redwood Dedicated for Aperture Labs' MVP. Goal is to run a customer-facing inference path for our image-to-text assist product. High level traffic we're planning for the pilot: average 450 requests/minute (7.5 rps) with occasional peaks up to ~3,000 requests/minute (50 rps) during flashes. Average prompt+response token footprint is ~1,200 tokens per request (we're conservative on length).

SLO: 95th percentile latency for end-to-end generation (model inference only) target <= 250 ms. We need a sizing recommendation (tokens/sec and GPU count) that meets the SLO with at least 2x burst headroom and a recommended canary rollout (how many GPUs to start with).

Tech stack: hoping to run a 13B/70B mixed strategy. For quality we prefer the 70B family for critical flows but can fall back to a quantized 13B for aggressive cost controls. We'll share an internal spreadsheet with traffic patterns (attached).

Ask: can you (1) estimate tokens/sec and GPU footprint for both model variants, (2) propose initial Dedicated slab size for pilot + 2x burst headroom, and (3) outline fallback routing & canary approach for latency-sensitive flows?

I've CC'd procurement (procurement@aperturelabs.com) to start the paperwork timeline when we're aligned.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@aperturelabs.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for our MVP pilot

Alex / team — ran through the spreadsheet and sketched a capacity model. Summary up front, then the math and recommendations.

Summary recommendations
- Pilot slab: 4 H100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale burst to 8 H100-equivalents. Rationale: meets p95 <= 250 ms for 13B quantized option and provides graceful fallback for 70B at reduced concurrency.
- Production target (if you commit to steady 50 rps sustained): 12 H100-equivalents to keep full 70B quality at target SLO with 2x headroom.
- Canary: start with 2 GPUs (13B quantized) routing 10% of traffic for 48 hours, then scale to 4 GPUs for 24-72 hours before broad rollout.

Assumptions used
- Average tokens/request (T) = 1,200 (prompt + gen) as provided.
- Peak RPS (R) = 50 requests/sec for flash events.
- Desired headroom factor (H) = 2x on tokens/sec.
- Effective tokens/sec requirement = R * T * H. For R=50: tokens/sec = 50 * 1,200 * 2 = 120,000 tokens/sec.

Model throughput estimates (empirical baselines from Redwood runtime tests):
- Llama2-13B (int8 optimized, KV caching enabled): ~18,000 tokens/sec per A100-class GPU under steady-state generation (short-circuit workloads reduce overhead).
- Llama2-13B (q4f16 on H100 runtime): ~28,000 tokens/sec per H100-equivalent (we measure H100 as ~1.5x A100 for these models).
- Llama2-70B (q4f16 on H100, aggressive kernel optimizations): ~9,000 tokens/sec per H100-equivalent at the sequence lengths you're targeting (1,200 tokens avg), because KV-cache and long sequence handling reduce throughput for large models.

Sizing math
- If you commit to serving 70B at target SLO with H=2: required H100-equivalents = ceil(120,000 / 9,000) = 14 GPUs. That's why production 70B with 2x headroom pushes to ~12-16 H100s depending on tail behavior.
- If you run quantized 13B as primary (13B q4 on H100): required H100-equiv = ceil(120,000 / 28,000) = 5 GPUs. We round down for pilot to 4 with autoscale to 8 for bursts (cost tradeoff + routing fallback to 70B for quality-critical requests).

Latency note and SLO fit
- The p95 inference latency budget target <= 250 ms is feasible on 13B quantized sizing above; for 70B at those token lengths p95 often slips during flash-start bursts if we don't provide larger slabs or warm KV caches. We recommend:
  - aggressive prefix / KV caching for repeated prompts
  - request-level routing: route highest-value sessions to pre-warmed 70B nodes, normal sessions to 13B quantized nodes
  - a short warm-up canary window and traffic shaping rules for the first 10 minutes of any flash event

Operational recommendations
- Autoscale policy: instant burst capacity (pre-authorized) up to +100% for 15 minutes, then throttle to +50% sustained.
- Canary funnel: 2 GPUs (13B) -> 4 GPUs -> 4 GPUs + up to 8 burst for traffic surges. When moving to 70B primary, scale to 12 GPUs gradually with traffic fractioning.
- Cost/capacity suggestion: start pilot with 4 H100-equiv slab and a 24/7 reserved warm pool of 1-2 GPUs to serve as a cache-warm pool.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_calc.csv includes the per-minute tokens/sec curves used for the ceil math. Happy to walk through the calc in a short call tomorrow.

—Ben
